headline: What to Do When Your Campaign Stops Converting
articleBody: Got a warm spot on your concrete floor? It's easy to just shrug it off, but that's one of the biggest mistakes you can make! Here are a few common missteps and how to sidestep them. First, don't ignore it. A warm spot almost always signals a hidden plumbing leak under your slab, and those don't fix themselves. Second, avoid DIY fixes if you're not a plumbing pro. Trying to chip away concrete or patch pipes without proper training can lead to bigger, more expensive problems, like damaging other utilities or the foundation itself. Third, don't wait for other symptoms to appear. While a high water bill or damp spots might eventually show up, the warm floor is your early warning sign. Delaying action allows the leak to worsen, potentially causing extensive water damage and mold growth. Fourth, guessing the location of the leak is futile. It’s hard to pinpoint exactly where the leak is without specialized equipment, so avoid unnecessary demolition. Lastly, don't choose an inexperienced plumber. Slab leaks require specific expertise and equipment for accurate detection and repair.
